chunks: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: “Whenever doubt enters upon you in your salat (prayer), act upon the greater number.” He said: “Then when you finish, complete what you think you omitted.” And whoever becomes certain that he added something in the salat (prayer), the repetition of the salat (prayer) becomes obligatory upon him. What indicates that is what he narrated:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Mu'adh ibn Muslim, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ ٱلصَّلَاةِ: repeating the salat (prayer) from the beginning
key_terms.زَادَ: added something extra to the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتِكَ: your salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being performed
key_terms.نَقَصْتَ: you omitted or fell short in the number of prayer units or acts
key_terms.ٱلشَّكِّ: doubt or uncertainty arising during the prayer
key_terms.ٱلْأَكْثَرِ: the greater number, meaning the higher count taken as the basis
key_terms.ٱنْصَرَفْتَ: you finished and departed from the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if doubt occurs in salat (prayer) about the number of units prayed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for doubt in salat (prayer): one should proceed on the basis of the greater number when uncertainty arises. It also states that if a person becomes certain that an addition was made in the prayer, repeating the prayer is obligatory.
